title: Salade de Lentilles
subtitle: A French Puy lentil salad with mustard vinaigrette
excerpt: Warm Puy lentils dressed with Dijon vinaigrette, shallot, and flat-leaf parsley. Served at room temperature, this works as a starter or a side to grilled meat.
sourceNotes: Classic French bistro lentil salad using Puy lentils, which hold their shape after cooking. Dijon vinaigrette is the standard dressing.

recipe.batchNotes: Cook a large batch of lentils and dress portions as needed. Dressed lentils keep well in the fridge for 2 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to a day ahead. Add parsley just before serving.

content.text: Puy lentils hold their shape and have enough flavour to carry a simple vinaigrette. Dress them while still warm so they absorb the dressing properly. Overcooking turns them to mush.
Put the lentils in the large saucepan with the bay leaves and thyme. Cover with cold water by 5cm. Do not salt the water yet.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook for 20 to 25 minutes until just tender but still holding their shape.
While the lentils cook, whisk the mustard, vinegar, salt, and pepper in the large bowl. Whisk in the olive oil until combined.
Drain the lentils and remove the bay and thyme. Tip the warm lentils straight into the bowl with the dressing.
Add the diced shallot and toss well. Leave to cool to room temperature for 10 minutes.
Stir in the parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve at room temperature.

items.cause: They cooked too long or the water was salted from the start.
items.fix: Salt cooking water only in the last 5 minutes. Begin checking at 18 minutes.

items.symptom: The salad tastes bland after resting.
items.cause: The lentils absorbed the vinaigrette and dulled the seasoning.
items.fix: Add a small splash of red wine vinegar and a pinch of salt before serving.

items.symptom: The dressing splits and looks oily.
items.cause: The oil was added too quickly.
items.fix: Whisk in the oil slowly in a thin stream. A teaspoon of water helps it emulsify.
